remaining: No abstract shell semantics or automatic command execution is claimed; terminal dispatch authority is covered separately.
evidenceDecision: Pure command resolution/catalogue and qualified draft tests cover aliases, key normalization and owner identity. The shared Chat composer DOM consumer covers native editing/completion, IME-safe Ctrl/Cmd+Enter send, multiline Enter, overflow command browsing, isolated drafts and transactional refusal restoration; source race tests cover native queued admission and unchecked slash-command receipts. History input and the mobile shell launcher share the single-submission lock and runtime-qualified draft. Composer DOM tests cover busy-agent confirmation, IME and touch release; the real History browser consumer checks runtime versus transport identity and retired-send draft restoration. Launcher DOM and TerminalView consumers check connection/pane replacement, empty-draft admission, explicit command selection and failed-send recovery. These are concrete editing/native-input contracts, so direct consumer evidence remains more useful than abstract shell semantics. Chat's ⋮ key controls reuse the configured Terminal shortcuts: the pure key-map test checks every Terminal control maps to a Herdr key name or is disabled, and the menu browser consumer checks the controls send only to the session Chat shows. Roamgate web sync through 2b16e991 (PR3): an isolated DOM consumer keeps unsent drafts across a same-destination reconnect, on the same pane and terminal, without writing browser storage; composer tests cover image-path sends that wait for the attachment, and the Option-as-Alt choice has direct storage evidence. Roamgate sync through bf3879f93: concrete isolated-DOM consumers cover pane-chat focus and questions, captured metadata scope and Vim editing; pure send/lock regressions cover every modified key and typed-text failure without restoration. The existing exhaustive dispatch/retirement checks cover runtime authority; no abstract shell semantics are added.
